habitat: Subtropical/tropical moist montane forests; evergreen broadleaf forest; and secondary growth
story: Few birds capture the imagination quite like the White Bellied Sea Eagle (Yuhina flavicollis). As a member of the Zosteropidae family, it has carved out a unique niche in Subtropical/tropical moist montane forests; evergreen broadleaf forest; and secondary growth. Its conservation status is Least Concern (LC), a classification that drives crucial research and protection efforts. The White Bellied Sea Eagle's presence is a vital sign of its ecosystem's health, making its preservation a priority. This poster is a tribute to the White Bellied Sea Eagle, celebrating its role in the natural world and inspiring a deeper appreciation for biodiversity.
